stories.title: Futures point to a gap higher for Black Friday's half-day; S&P 500 E-mini +1.56%
stories.body: At about 7:33 AM ET the S&P 500 E-mini was 7,307.75 (+1.56%), the Nasdaq-100 future 26,655.75 (+2.13%) and the Dow future 50,874 (+1.29%) (JBizNews). Yahoo Finance said chip stocks rebounded as nerves over AI profitability eased. Wednesday's cash close: S&P 500 7,182.78 (−0.25%), Nasdaq 23,585.80 (−0.62%), Dow 50,182.95 (+0.33%); on Wednesday's close the S&P 500 was up nearly 4% for the week (TipRanks). Stocks close at 1:00 PM ET and bonds at 2:00 PM.
stories.why: A gap of this size opens far from Wednesday's last 1-hour candle, and the half-day leaves only about three completed 1-hour closes before the weekend to show whether it holds.

stories.title: Apple leads the megacaps year to date; Tesla sits 22% below its peak
stories.body: Through Wednesday's close Apple was up 30.8% this year, Amazon 5.9%, Meta −7.6% and Tesla −15.5% (TokenPost). On Wednesday Meta rose 3.4%, Apple 0.4%, Amazon fell 3.1% and Tesla 1.2% (TheStreet). Tesla's $380.14 close left it 22.40% below its Dec. 16, 2025 peak of $489.88, and JournalArta noted reports that Tesla and SpaceX are deepening talks on an all-stock merger. Upstox listed Amazon and Alphabet among names rallying before Friday's open.
stories.why: Megacaps carry most of the index weight, so whether they join the chip-led gap decides how much of it shows up in SPY's and QQQ's 1-hour closes.

stories.title: Chips lead the pre-market rebound: Micron +5% after a 13% intraday drop Wednesday
stories.body: Micron rose 5% before the bell (Yahoo Finance), and Upstox listed AMD, Broadcom and Intel among the chip names rallying pre-market. Wednesday closes: MU $601.25 (−4.53%), AMD $406.03 (−1.75%), AVGO $300.86 (−0.07%), INTC $54.47 (−0.60%) (us-market-data). Overnight, chip shares led Tokyo: Advantest +7.07%, Tokyo Electron +4.43%, Kioxia +8.86% (NERO, citing Reuters), and Infineon was up 3.64% in Frankfurt on Friday (Trading Economics).
stories.why: Wednesday's lows were 10–13% below the prior close for MU, AMD and INTC; a gap up meets the overhead supply left by Tuesday's and Wednesday's 1-hour candles.

stories.title: Brent settles +2.07% Thursday after a strike on Aramco's Jazan refinery; banks ended Wednesday flat
stories.body: Brent settled at $96.57 on Thursday, up $1.96 (2.07%); there was no US settlement because of Thanksgiving (The Nation). A projectile struck Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery Thursday, halting some operations (Reuters via BOE Report). Wednesday closes: CVX $210.95 (+1.06%), XOM $158.08 (−0.09%), JPM $316.74 (−0.11%), BAC $48.54 (−0.04%) (us-market-data). The 10-year yield was back at 4.91% Friday morning from 4.86% (Saxo).
stories.why: Energy names reopen with two days of oil moves to price at once, so the first 1-hour candle may gap; banks have no stock-specific news and tend to track yields.

stories.title: Nvidia up more than 2% pre-market as Bloomberg reports Blackwell racks at a Shanghai site
stories.body: Nvidia rose more than 2% before the bell after closing Wednesday at $149.30 (−3.91%) (Yahoo Finance). Bloomberg reported that two Chinese firms installed Blackwell-based hardware, including a GB300 NVL72 rack pledged as collateral for a 96 million yuan loan, at a Shanghai data center tied to Megaspeed-linked companies (Investing.com). Blackwell chips require a US export license for China; Megaspeed, added to the Entity List on Nov. 23, says it conducts lawful business, and Bloomberg found no evidence it diverted the hardware itself (Roic.ai).
stories.why: NVDA swung +31.5%, −5.86% and −3.91% in three sessions; implied volatility stays high, so even a half-day can produce wide 1-hour ranges around the gap.

stories.title: Gold rebounds to about $3,650 and silver jumps 6% in thin post-holiday trade
stories.body: Spot gold was $3,640.84 (+2.1%) at 06:09 GMT, up about 3.1% for the week, as forced selling paused and the dollar index eased to 103.72 (Reuters via ANC). FinanceFeeds had spot gold at $3,650.08 at 06:45 GMT, February COMEX gold at $3,678.40 and spot silver up 6.2% at $44.07 (CNBC); spot gold hit $3,445.89 on Wednesday, its lowest since August 2025. GLD closed Wednesday at $327.45 (+0.61%) and SLV at $37.10 (+0.71%).
stories.why: GLD and SLV last traded Wednesday, so both are set to gap up toward the overnight metal moves; the first completed 1-hour close shows whether the gap is accepted.

stories.title: Iran's Guards claim two tankers hit mines near Khasab; Brent heads for its first weekly gain in four
stories.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting mines north of Oman's Khasab port; maritime agencies have not independently confirmed the claim (Energy News Beat). The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed four drones the Houthis aimed at Ras Tanura and did not confirm refinery damage. Brent settled Thursday at $96.57 (+2.07%) (The Nation), and WTI was $85.78 (+2.5% from Wednesday's settle) early Friday, with oil on track to snap a three-week losing streak (Reuters via BOE Report). OPEC+ meets Sunday and is expected to hold output targets through at least Q1 2027, two sources said.
stories.why: USO and OXY reopen after a holiday in which Brent kept trading, and the OPEC+ meeting falls on Sunday, after Friday's last completed 1-hour close.

stories.title: VIX eases to 26.80 overnight; the curve stays in backwardation
stories.body: The VIX was 26.80 at 05:00 CET, down 5.27% from Wednesday's 28.29 close. December VIX futures were 23.73 and January 23.32, leaving the front month 3.07 points below spot. The SKEW index was 142.06 and S&P 500 20-day realized volatility 30.91; Saxo labeled the regime "high vol bear" (Saxo).
stories.why: Backwardation means near-dated options still price more movement than later ones; premiums stay expensive even on a rally day.

stories.title: 10-year yield back near 4.91%; futures price a 99.4% chance of a December hike
stories.body: The 10-year Treasury yield was 4.91% Friday morning, up from 4.86%, and the 2-year 4.68% (Saxo); CNBC had the 10-year at 4.918% at 06:44 GMT (FinanceFeeds). Futures price a 99.4% chance of a 25 bp hike at the Dec. 8–9 Fed meeting (Mitrade via FinanceFeeds). On Wednesday the 10-year fell 6 bp to 4.86%, its eighth straight daily decline, with FedWatch at 97% (TheStreet). The bond market closes at 2:00 PM ET.
stories.why: Rising yields alongside a stock gap up is a mixed signal; rate-sensitive names can lag the index in the 1-hour closes.

stories.title: KOSPI +4.34%, Shanghai +3.73% as Asia's chip rebound spreads; Europe extends gains
stories.body: Friday closes: Nikkei 225 58,711.11 (+2.11%), KOSPI 4,915.68 (+4.34%), Shanghai Composite 3,606.49 (+3.73%), Hang Seng 22,708.97 (+2.17%) (NERO). Beijing pledged at midday to channel more long-term capital into stocks (Trading Economics), and Tokyo core CPI rose 2.9% vs 3.0% expected. In Europe the DAX closed Thursday +2.08% at 25,216 (Trading Economics) after milder-than-feared US tariff proposals (JournalArta) and was +0.59% Friday morning.
stories.why: Asian chip names reversed Wednesday's rout before the US open, which is part of why US chip futures are gapping higher.

stories.title: October goods trade deficit widens to $149.5B vs $133.1B expected
stories.body: The advance goods trade deficit was $149.5 billion in October vs $133.1 billion expected and $135.1 billion in September, as imports rose 6.1% to $365.3 billion and capital goods imports 8.5% to $171.4 billion. Wholesale inventories rose 0.9% vs 0.5% expected, and retail inventories rose 0.8% (ActionForex). Before the data, the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow was 2.9% for Q4, down from 3.2% (TipRanks). On Thanksgiving, President Trump called the revised 4.3% Q3 GDP figure "fake" (Yahoo Finance, citing Bloomberg).
stories.why: A wider deficit subtracts from GDP estimates; with a December hike already almost fully priced, the data matter more for yields than for the open.

stories.title: Today's S&P 500 expiry priced about ±1.37%; futures already sit above the week's option-priced range
stories.body: At Wednesday's close, options priced about a 1.37% (98.40-point) move for today's S&P 500 expiry, centred near 7,185, and the week's option-priced range was 6,636.99–7,183.79; futures at 7,315.25 were about 118 points above its top (Saxo). Doublewide Capital put the half-day-adjusted implied move at ±80.25 E-mini points. Nvidia's IV rank was 92.2 and the US median IV rank 57.1 (Saxo). Index options settle at the 1:00 PM ET close.
stories.why: Contracts expiring today have only a half-day left; a gap beyond the priced range shifts which strikes are in the money before the first 1-hour close prints.

stories.title: Ahead: 1:00 PM close today, OPEC+ on Sunday, the Fed and Broadcom on Dec. 9
stories.body: Stocks close at 1:00 PM ET today, eligible options at 1:15 PM and bonds at 2:00 PM (FedRateCalc). OPEC+ ministers meet Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 PM GMT (The Nation), and January Brent expires Nov. 30 (Saxo). BOJ Governor Ueda speaks Monday (NERO). Jensen Huang testifies before Congress next week (Yahoo Finance). The Fed decides Dec. 9 (Saxo), the day Broadcom reports after the close (Broadcom IR). Final action on the proposed Section 301 tariffs could come as early as January (Bloomberg via News Tribune).
stories.why: Weekend events (OPEC+) land after Friday's last completed 1-hour close, so Monday's first candle is where any reaction shows.

tone.text: Risk-on into a half-day: futures point to a gap higher led by chips (Micron +5%, Nvidia +2% pre-market), Asia closed sharply higher (KOSPI +4.34%, Shanghai +3.73%) and the VIX eased to 26.80 overnight, while oil and gold climbed and the 10-year yield rose back to about 4.91%.

futures.text: Pre-market (about 7:33 AM ET): S&P 500 E-mini 7,307.75 (+1.56%), Nasdaq-100 26,655.75 (+2.13%), Dow 50,874 (+1.29%). Stocks close at 1:00 PM ET and bonds at 2:00 PM today.

global.note: Asia closed sharply higher as chip shares rebounded (Advantest +7.07%, Tokyo Electron +4.43%) and Beijing pledged market support; Tokyo core CPI rose 2.9% vs 3.0% expected. Europe extended Thursday's rally, when the DAX closed +2.08% and the CAC 40 +1.61% (Trading Economics).
